newsitem.title: USA: American Air pilots reject labor contract.
newsitem.headline: American Air pilots reject labor contract.

text.p: The Allied Pilots Association (APA) said on Wednesday its members rejected a new four-year labor contract with AMR Corp's American Airlines.
APA spokesman Gregg Overman said in a recorded message that 5,046 members voted against ratifying the proposed contract, compared with 3,197 in favor.
"Therefore, by a majority vote of 61.2 percent, the tentative agreement has failed," Overman said.
American Airlines officials were not immediately available for comment. The airline had said it would only go through with a planned overhaul of its fleet if pilots approved the new contract.
In November, American Airlines pledged to buy 103 jets from Boeing Co. and take out options on 527 more in one of the biggest commerical airplane orders in history.
But the airline said the deal was contingent on pilots accepting the labor contract, which provided for a 3 percent wage increase in August 1997, and another 2 percent raise in August 1999.
The APA board of directors had approved the new labor contract in November, and had recommended that members follow suit.
Overman said the union's board of directors would meet in Fort Worth on Thursday to discuss their next step.
